housing: South Holland is a flat, low-lying fenland district centred on Spalding, with farming and food processing as the main employers. Homes are mostly brick-built terraces, bungalows and post-war and new-build estates, with Georgian houses in the centres of Spalding and Long Sutton. Private renting grew quickly between 2011 and 2021, much of it shared and family houses let to workers in agriculture and food factories. Most of the district is below sea level at high tide and relies on drainage boards.
checkinTips: Shared houses let to farm and factory workers: photograph each bedroom lock, fire doors, smoke alarms and the shared kitchen, and note the number of occupiers.
Homes on low-lying fenland: check ground floors, skirting boards and gardens for damp or past flooding, and photograph drains and soakaways.
Bungalows and older houses on peat or clay soils: photograph any cracks in walls, door frames that stick and uneven floors, which may come from ground movement.
Rural homes off the gas grid: record the oil tank and gauge level or LPG tank, and any septic tank or treatment plant cover.
New-build estates around Spalding and Holbeach: photograph snagging items, sealant, paintwork and the garden.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems can contact South Holland District Council's private sector housing team, which can inspect homes and take action against landlords.
